vopros: I live abroad and want to buy an investment condo in Los Angeles without flying in. Which agents handle the whole purchase remotely?

vyzhimka.tekst:
Yes. Based on their published services, these are reasonable Los Angeles-area candidates to contact:

### Agents and teams advertising remote/international purchases

- **Saman Alishahi — Keller Williams, Beverly Hills**  
  Specifically advertises out-of-state and international purchases, live video walkthroughs, digital signing, local inspection coordination, and foreign-national financing.  
  **DRE #01964365** · +1 310-849-9898 · samkw310@gmail.com

- **David S. Blumberg — Los Angeles**  
  Focuses on residential and investment properties, including condos, and states that he works with U.S. and foreign nationals.  
  **DRE #01079569** · 818-856-1415 · David@DavidSBlumberg.com

- **Brian Cooper — Cooper Family Real Estate**  
  Advertises remote purchases for buyers in the UK, Canada, Australia, and elsewhere, including virtual tours, inspections, negotiation, power-of-attorney coordination, and remote signing logistics.

- **Christina Pope / Elite Residence International**  
  Focuses on international Los Angeles buyers and discusses remote tours, cross-border funds, identity verification, and investment purchases.  
  **310-404-9931**

- **Antola Properties**  
  International-focused brokerage serving coastal Los Angeles and explicitly discusses buying remotely through electronic signing, U.S. consulate notarization, or an appropriate power of attorney.

- **French Cluster / Corinne Allemand**  
  A potentially useful option if you speak French. The service specifically mentions foreign purchasers and residential investment properties, including condos, throughout Los Angeles.

- **The Agency, Sally Forster Jones Group, and Briggs Freeman**  
  Larger luxury-oriented organizations with virtual consultations, remote tours, electronic offers, and remote transaction support. Ask to be assigned an agent experienced specifically with **international investment-condo buyers**, rather than a general relocation agent.

### What “whole purchase remotely” should include

Ask each agent to confirm, in writing, that they will handle:

1. MLS search and investment-oriented property screening  
2. Live video tours and neighborhood/street-noise checks  
3. Review of condo disclosures, HOA budgets, reserves, litigation, insurance, rental rules, and special assessments  
4. Comparable-sales and rental-income analysis  
5. Offer preparation, negotiation, and electronic signatures  
6. In-person inspection, sewer/plumbing/HVAC checks where relevant, and video reporting  
7. Coordination with escrow, title, lender, insurance broker, property manager, and attorney  
8. Remote signing or an acceptable power-of-attorney process  
9. Key handoff, tenant placement, and ongoing property management after closing

For an **investment condo**, the HOA review is especially important. Require the agent to obtain and help you analyze the CC&Rs, recent meeting minutes, reserve study, budget, insurance, pending assessments, rental caps, minimum lease terms, short-term-rental restrictions, owner-occupancy ratio, and litigation.

### Important remote-closing caution

Do not assume “online closing” means California notaries can simply notarize everything by video. California generally still requires physical appearance before a California notary; some transactions can use an out-of-state remote-online notary, a mobile/mail-away signing, a U.S. consulate notary, or a properly drafted power of attorney. The **escrow company, title underwriter, and lender—not just the agent—must approve the exact method in advance**.

Also use an independent California real-estate attorney and a U.S. tax adviser familiar with foreign owners. A foreign buyer generally can purchase the condo, but ownership structure, U.S. tax filings, withholding, estate tax, financing, and eventual sale require professional advice. FIRPTA primarily concerns withholding when a foreign owner later sells; escrow should still explain all applicable seller-withholding procedures in the transaction.

### Message to send prospective agents

> I live outside the United States and want to buy a Los Angeles investment condo without visiting before closing. Do you personally handle international remote purchases? Please describe your process for live video tours, HOA and rental-rule review, inspections, investment analysis, electronic offers, escrow, notarization or power of attorney, financing, insurance, property management, and post-closing tenant placement. How many comparable transactions have you completed in the last two years, and can you provide your California DRE license number and references?

I would interview at least three candidates and choose the one who can identify a specific escrow/title company, inspector, lender or foreign-national financing specialist, attorney, and property manager before you sign a buyer-broker agreement.

results.snippet:
Withholding When the Seller is a Foreign Person: Under federal law, a buyer of real estate is obligated to 
withhold 15% of the purchase price and forward that amount to the Internal Revenue Service IF the seller is a 
foreign person.
The law applies to all sales of real property in the United States, residential and commercial,
whether maintained for personal use or investment.
The withholding amount is reduced to 10% if the buyer will be 
an owner occupant and the purchase price is $1 million or less.
Penalties: A buyer who fails to withhold when required, may be liable for the amount of the tax, plus interest and
penalties, if the seller is a foreign person and does not pay taxes on the sale.
Exemptions:  The buyer need not withhold if they obtain any one of the four exemptions applies:  
• 
One – The Buyer’s Affidavit.
The buyer may sign an affidavit affirming the buyer’s intent to occupy the
property as a residence and that the purchase price does not exceed $300,000.
Use C.A.R.
Form AB;  
• 
Two – The Seller’s Affidavit.
The seller may provide an affidavit to the buyer asserting the seller is not a 
foreign person AND the affidavit contains the seller’s social security number or taxpayer ID.
C.A.R.
Form AS
may be used;  
• 
Three – The Qualified Substitute.
Instead of providing the buyer with an AS (which contains the seller’s Tax 
ID), the seller may provide a completed affidavit to a title or escrow company (qualified substitute) who in 
turn provides the buyer with an affidavit affirming the qualified substitute is in possession of the seller’s
completed affidavit asserting that no withholding is required; OR  
• 
Four – IRS Withholding Statement: Although rarely done, the seller may provide the buyer with a statement 
from the IRS showing that no withholding is required.
...
If the buyer does not receive a fully completed Form AS from the seller, or a Form QS, or equivalent, from the title or
escrow company, the buyer should instruct escrow to withhold funds to forward to the IRS and talk to an attorney 
about the implications to the transaction.

Remote online notarization (RON) involves a notary public performing a notarial act using audio-visual technology over the internet.
Instead of meeting in person, the signer and notary connect through a secure online platform.
This technology allows for identity verification, document signing, and the application of a digital notary seal and signature, all conducted remotely.
...
California has adopted a phased approach to implementing remote online notarization.
...
However, California law does recognize notarizations performed by notaries commissioned in other states that do permit RON.
This means that if you are in Los Angeles and need a document notarized for a real estate transaction, you can utilize an out-of-state remote online notary, and the notarization will generally be accepted in California, provided it complies with the laws of the state where the notary is commissioned.
The full implementation allowing California notaries to perform RONs is anticipated by January 1, 2030, or earlier, upon the California Secretary of State’s completion of a required technology project.

Yes. Based on their published services, these are reasonable Los Angeles-area candidates to contact:

### Agents and teams advertising remote/international purchases

- **Saman Alishahi — Keller Williams, Beverly Hills**  
  Specifically advertises out-of-state and international purchases, live video walkthroughs, digital signing, local inspection coordination, and foreign-national financing.  
  **DRE #01964365** · +1 310-849-9898 · samkw310@gmail.com

- **David S. Blumberg — Los Angeles**  
  Focuses on residential and investment properties, including condos, and states that he works with U.S. and foreign nationals.  
  **DRE #01079569** · 818-856-1415 · David@DavidSBlumberg.com

- **Brian Cooper — Cooper Family Real Estate**  
  Advertises remote purchases for buyers in the UK, Canada, Australia, and elsewhere, including virtual tours, inspections, negotiation, power-of-attorney coordination, and remote signing logistics.

- **Christina Pope / Elite Residence International**  
  Focuses on international Los Angeles buyers and discusses remote tours, cross-border funds, identity verification, and investment purchases.  
  **310-404-9931**

- **Antola Properties**  
  International-focused brokerage serving coastal Los Angeles and explicitly discusses buying remotely through electronic signing, U.S. consulate notarization, or an appropriate power of attorney.

- **French Cluster / Corinne Allemand**  
  A potentially useful option if you speak French. The service specifically mentions foreign purchasers and residential investment properties, including condos, throughout Los Angeles.

- **The Agency, Sally Forster Jones Group, and Briggs Freeman**  
  Larger luxury-oriented organizations with virtual consultations, remote tours, electronic offers, and remote transaction support. Ask to be assigned an agent experienced specifically with **international investment-condo buyers**, rather than a general relocation agent.

### What “whole purchase remotely” should include

Ask each agent to confirm, in writing, that they will handle:

1. MLS search and investment-oriented property screening  
2. Live video tours and neighborhood/street-noise checks  
3. Review of condo disclosures, HOA budgets, reserves, litigation, insurance, rental rules, and special assessments  
4. Comparable-sales and rental-income analysis  
5. Offer preparation, negotiation, and electronic signatures  
6. In-person inspection, sewer/plumbing/HVAC checks where relevant, and video reporting  
7. Coordination with escrow, title, lender, insurance broker, property manager, and attorney  
8. Remote signing or an acceptable power-of-attorney process  
9. Key handoff, tenant placement, and ongoing property management after closing

For an **investment condo**, the HOA review is especially important. Require the agent to obtain and help you analyze the CC&Rs, recent meeting minutes, reserve study, budget, insurance, pending assessments, rental caps, minimum lease terms, short-term-rental restrictions, owner-occupancy ratio, and litigation.

### Important remote-closing caution

Do not assume “online closing” means California notaries can simply notarize everything by video. California generally still requires physical appearance before a California notary; some transactions can use an out-of-state remote-online notary, a mobile/mail-away signing, a U.S. consulate notary, or a properly drafted power of attorney. The **escrow company, title underwriter, and lender—not just the agent—must approve the exact method in advance**.

Also use an independent California real-estate attorney and a U.S. tax adviser familiar with foreign owners. A foreign buyer generally can purchase the condo, but ownership structure, U.S. tax filings, withholding, estate tax, financing, and eventual sale require professional advice. FIRPTA primarily concerns withholding when a foreign owner later sells; escrow should still explain all applicable seller-withholding procedures in the transaction.

### Message to send prospective agents

> I live outside the United States and want to buy a Los Angeles investment condo without visiting before closing. Do you personally handle international remote purchases? Please describe your process for live video tours, HOA and rental-rule review, inspections, investment analysis, electronic offers, escrow, notarization or power of attorney, financing, insurance, property management, and post-closing tenant placement. How many comparable transactions have you completed in the last two years, and can you provide your California DRE license number and references?

I would interview at least three candidates and choose the one who can identify a specific escrow/title company, inspector, lender or foreign-national financing specialist, attorney, and property manager before you sign a buyer-broker agreement.
